title: Tight Parallel Repetition for Private-Coin Arguments
authors: Zvika Brakerski, Andrew Huang, Yael Tauman Kalai, Nicholas Spooner
abstract: We show that assuming the existence of homomorphic encryption, parallel repetition of all interactive arguments (after being run under homomorphic encryption) reduces the soundness error at a tight exponential rate even in the post-quantum setting. Moreover, we generalize this result to hold for threshold verifiers, where the parallel repeated verifier accepts if and only if at least $t$ of the executions are accepted (for some threshold $t$). Prior to this work, these results were known only when the cheating prover was assumed to be classical, and it was not known how to achieve tight bounds.   As a corollary, we construct the first constant-round succinct argument for $\mathsf{QMA}$ with negligible completeness and soundness errors assuming only the existence of quantum homomorphic encryption.
summary: This theoretical paper advances the field of quantum interactive proofs by demonstrating that parallel repetition can achieve tight exponential reduction of soundness error for private-coin arguments, even in the post-quantum regime. By assuming the existence of quantum homomorphic encryption, the authors construct a highly efficient, constant-round succinct argument for the QMA complexity class. This work significantly tightens the theoretical bounds for quantum verification protocols.
main_problem: The paper aims to improve the soundness error reduction for private-coin interactive arguments in the quantum setting, particularly by leveraging parallel repetition.
main_result: They show that parallel repetition reduces the soundness error at a tight exponential rate, leading to the construction of the first constant-round succinct argument for QMA assuming quantum homomorphic encryption.
method: The core method involves transforming the argument using Homomorphic Encryption (HE) and then applying techniques like direct-product repetition and Quantum Singular Value Transformation (QSVT) to manage quantum state entanglement across repetitions.
model_or_system: The analysis is based on computationally sound interactive arguments $\langle P, V angle$ and their transformation $\langle bP, bV angle$ using a quantum homomorphic encryption scheme (QHE).

important_parameters: Number of repetitions ($k$), threshold ($t$), security parameter ($\lambda$), and initial soundness error ($\epsilon$).
main_assumptions: Existence of post-quantum Homomorphic Encryption (HE) and the ability to perform quantum state manipulations like QSVT.
